content: The guideline development process involved technical contributions from various WHO staff members, including Rachel Albone and Matteo Cesari from the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child & Adolescent Health and Ageing at WHO Headquarters. Tarun Dua, Gilles Forte, Benedikt Huttner, Dzmitry Krupchanka, Vladimir Poznyak, Pura Solon, Wouter ‘t Hoen, Rebekah Thomas, and Mark van Ommeren also provided input, representing departments such as Mental Health and Substance Use, Access to Medicines and Health Products, Health Products Policy and Standards, and Quality Assurance, Norms, and Standards at WHO Headquarters. Administrative support was provided by George Davis, Liying Huang, and Pascale Pomoshchnick from the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child & Adolescent Health and Ageing. WHO acknowledges the advice received from Cochrane Musculoskeletal during the planning stage of the guideline. Financial support was provided by the governments of Canada, Germany, Japan, and the Kanagawa prefectural government in Japan. The funding bodies had no influence on the content or recommendations of the guideline. Editing was carried out by Iain Bamforth. The guideline includes a glossary of terms and abbreviations. For example, assistive products are defined as external devices that maintain or improve an individual’s functioning and independence, such as lumbar braces or mobility aids like wheelchairs and crutches. The biopsychosocial model refers to the interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing chronic primary low back pain (CPLBP). This approach emphasizes addressing these factors in a person-centered manner. CPLBP is defined as pain persisting or recurring for more than three months without being attributable to another diagnosis, such as a structural lesion or disease process. Emotional distress or functional disability criteria were not applied in this definition. Health practitioners are defined as individuals with health-related qualifications, encompassing both professionals and associate professionals. Health workers are those primarily engaged in actions aimed at enhancing health. Herbal medicines are products containing active ingredients derived from plants or plant materials. Injectable local anesthetics involve the delivery of anesthetic agents into the lower back’s soft tissues, excluding the spinal region. Intrinsic capacity refers to the composite of an individual’s physical and mental capacities. Massage therapy involves manual manipulation of soft tissues to improve health and well-being, including traditional, complementary, and integrative approaches. Multicomponent biopsychosocial care integrates at least two components of the biopsychosocial model (physical, psychological, or social) and is delivered by a single provider or multidisciplinary team. This approach aims to optimize function and reduce disability in individuals with health conditions interacting with their environment. Needling therapies include traditional Chinese medicine acupuncture and other dry needling modalities, such as myofascial trigger point needling and Western medical acupuncture. These involve inserting needles into specific points to address pain. A placebo is a comparator group in clinical trials, often used to test the benefits and harms of a treatment. Participants in the placebo group receive an intervention designed to mimic the actual treatment without its therapeutic effects. Psychological interventions include operant, respondent, cognitive, cognitive-behavioral, and mindfulness-based stress reduction therapies. These interventions target behavioral, physiological, and cognitive aspects of pain. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) integrates components of operant, respondent, and cognitive therapies to reduce pain and distress. Mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) focuses on developing non-judgmental, moment-by-moment awareness to reduce stress. Spinal manipulative therapy involves hands-on treatment of spinal joints, including mobilization (low-velocity, small or large amplitude movements) and manipulation (high-velocity thrusts). Sham interventions mimic the studied treatment without delivering the actual intervention, such as disabling the ultrasonic wave in sham ultrasound. Standardized mean difference (SMD) is a statistical measure used in meta-analyses to standardize outcomes measured differently across studies. Structured education and advice aim to improve understanding of pain and guide self-management. Structured exercise therapies involve planned, repetitive physical activities prescribed by health workers to improve physical fitness and reduce pain. Therapeutic ultrasound delivers sonic energy to deep tissues to increase temperature and promote healing. Traction applies a distraction force along the spine’s axis using body weight, weights, or pulleys, delivered in various forms and durations. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) uses electrical currents to stimulate nerves and manage pain.
